input_text: All patient records have been pseudonymized by the hospital IT department prior to being made available for this study. The original identifiers are stored in a separate key file which is not accessible to this system.

Data has been fully anonymized. All direct and indirect identifiers have been removed and k-anonymity with k=5 has been verified by our data governance team. Re-identification is not reasonably possible.
The dataset contains raw patient records including names, dates of birth, and national identification numbers. No processing has been applied to identifying fields.
All participants have provided written informed consent for their data to be used in federated learning research. Consent was obtained using the standard ethics-approved form.
This dataset is derived from routine clinical care records. The data is highly sensitive as it contains oncology diagnoses, treatment histories, and genomic profiles.
The dataset consists of aggregated hospital admission counts by month and region. No individual patient data is present. Sensitivity is minimal.
Records have had names and addresses removed but still contain age, postcode district, and diagnosis codes which could in combination re-identify individuals in small populations.
Our institution is legally required under the national health data act to contribute anonymised records to approved research registries. Participation in this study is covered by that obligation.

Patient identifiers have been replaced with pseudonyms using a one-way hash function maintained by our data steward. The mapping table is held in a separate secure environment outside the scope of this project.
This is a lightly processed version of the raw survey responses. Some free-text fields have been redacted but numeric scores and demographic categories remain. The data carries moderate sensitivity.

We have a legitimate interest in processing this data as part of our ongoing quality improvement programme. The processing is proportionate and participants have been informed through our standard privacy notice.
All variables in this dataset are computed statistics: means, standard deviations, and prevalence rates. The underlying individual records are never exported from the hospital system.
The dataset contains raw genomic sequencing data linked to patient clinical outcomes. This is highly sensitive personal health data subject to special category protections under GDPR Article 9.
Processing is necessary to protect the vital interests of patients in emergency care scenarios where consent cannot be obtained in time.
Patient records have been de-identified according to HIPAA Safe Harbor method. All 18 identifier categories have been removed.
This data was collected as part of routine hospital administration. We process it under our mandate as a public health authority to monitor and improve population health outcomes.
The data is a general population survey about lifestyle habits including diet and exercise. No medical or clinical data is included. We consider it low sensitivity.
We store patient data securely and follow all applicable regulations. The data is used for internal quality improvement only.
